seoul-south-korea-ganghwa-island-coastal.story: A rider’s loop: clean exit, memorable middle, calm return. 461 km round from Hwado - plan on about 9 h 36 of riding. seoul-south-korea-ganghwa-island-coastal.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: Scenic stretch near Gwangju → High point near Osan is the technical section. Hairpins, gradients and mixed traffic can stack up quickly; use low drama inputs, stay wide of centre lines and expect buses or riders appearing exactly where optimism says they will not.

This High point near Osan → Photo stop near Hwaseong-si stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

Photo stop near Hwaseong-si → Food stop near Kaesŏng can flow quickly, but only if you keep village limits and junction sightlines sacred. Fast connectors are where rides get untidy when fatigue creeps in.

safetyMarkers.note: Respect posted limits and assume enforcement near villages, viewpoints and main-road joins.
A line-crossing or merge area where relaxed sightseeing traffic can behave unpredictably.
Watch shade, leaves, gravel wash and damp patches; conditions decide the pace.

scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 59 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.
